answer: To resist Sybil attacks, agents register through a trusted identity kernel, tying each agent to an on-chain identity tree. When agents bridge identity across ecosystems, they publish a zero-knowledge nullifier plume derived from unique cryptographic attestation chains. Each additional concurrent identity registered by a single operator scales collateral quadratically (O(n^2)), inflicting exponential capital exhaustion that makes deploying a Sybil swarm economically impossible.
